subject: Intermittent large-response failures via Sparrow private peering — proxy + fragment drops
messages:
From: Sam Richards <sam.richards@sparrowlabs.io>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: netops@sparrowlabs.io
Date: 2026-09-02T07:45:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent failures for large inference responses to our private endpoint

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing intermittent client failures on our internal apps when the inference responses exceed ~1300 bytes. The errors look like stalled downloads or TCP resets mid-transfer. Small payloads are fine. This began after we put an HTTP forward-proxy in front of our app fleet (policy rollout last week).

Attached is a firewall-side pcap from the app VLAN and a quick topology sketch showing our proxy chain and the Redwood private peering. Can you advise?

Quick notes:
- Client range: 10.8.12.0/24
- Private peering via Orbital Transit (VXLAN) -> Redwood edge -> Redwood private VPC
- Observed ICMP "fragmentation needed" and also occasional TCP RSTs after retransmits.

Thanks,
Sam Richards
SRE, Sparrow Labs

Attachments: sparrow-fw-inside-20260902.pcap (pcap), sparrow-topology-sketch.pdf (pdf)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: sam.richards@sparrowlabs.io
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures for large inference responses to our private endpoint

Sam

Thanks for the captures and sketch. Looping in network team and AM. Initial questions while we triage:
- Do your proxy boxes perform TCP proxying/termination (i.e., they reassemble and open a separate downstream connection)?
- Any MTU or overlay changes in the Orbital Transit handoff recently? VXLAN adds ~50 bytes; we typically see issues when MSS isn't clamped.

Vivek: my first pass will check for fragments arriving at our edge and whether Orbital or the proxy are dropping fragments. If the proxy terminates TCP and performs a new TCP session, that can cause different MSS negotiation and force fragmentation mid-path.

Marissa: please flag this as high for Sparrow.

Soojin Lee
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, sam.richards@sparrowlabs.io
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures for large inference responses to our private endpoint

I've pulled the pcap. Highlights:
- I see "ICMP Frag Needed (DF set)" for flows with MSS negotiated at 1460. The ICMPs report path MTU around 1384 on some segments.
- There are groups of packets where fragments should be created but we do not observe fragments reaching the firewall inside interface; instead connections retry and some return RSTs.
- Notably, some return packets show a different source IP (SNAT pool gateway B) compared to the original SNAT gateway A; that suggests ECMP/policy-failover is sending return traffic via a different transit device and breaking conntrack on the firewall/proxy chain.

Immediate recommendations:
1) On Redwood egress for Sparrow prefix, apply MSS clamp to 1360 to cover VXLAN + proxy headers as a temporary mitigation.
2) Ask Orbital Transit whether they drop fragments or reassembly is disabled (many transit boxes drop fragments for security).
3) If Sparrow proxy terminates TLS and initiates new downstream connections, verify that it preserves MSS on the downstream path or performs MSS clamping.

I'll also sync conntrack logs and SNAT allocations to confirm asymmetric egress.

-Vivek Kulkarni
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: infra-support@orbital-transit.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, sam.richards@sparrowlabs.io
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures for large inference responses to our private endpoint

Hi all,
Orbital checked config: we do not reassemble fragments on transit; by default we drop non-first fragments if DF isn't set but fragments arrive mid-path. We also have an ECMP pair for Sparrow's egress and a failover policy that can change source NAT gateway based on load. We can open an allowance to pass fragments for the Sparrow peering prefix if you prefer.

Regards,
Orbital Transit Support

From: sam.richards@sparrowlabs.io
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: infra-support@orbital-transit.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-03T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures for large inference responses to our private endpoint

Team

Our proxy stack does perform TLS termination and then re-creates a downstream connection toward client VMs. Proxy vendor confirms downstream side uses standard MSS but doesn't clamp by default. We can enable proxy-side MSS clamp if that is recommended.

Orbital: please do open the fragment pass for the Sparrow prefix as a short-term change so we can observe behavior.

I'll schedule a maintenance window for the change; suggested window 2026-09-03 09:30-10:00 PT. Marissa please confirm this works for Redwood changes too.

Thanks,
Sam

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sam.richards@sparrowlabs.io
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-03T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Maintenance window confirmed  Sparrow private peering

Confirmed: Redwood will apply MSS clamp to 1360 at 09:35 PT and pin egress for Sparrow return flows to the primary Orbital gateway during the 30-minute window. Expected behaviour: in-flight large transfers may reset but should recover with the new MSS; this is same mitigation we use for VXLAN-overlay tenants.

I will update JIRA INF-1489 with runbook and rollback steps. Markus, please monitor for any cross-tenant impact.

-Marissa Cole
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, sam.richards@sparrowlabs.io
Date: 2026-09-04T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-maintenance summary: MSS clamp and egress pinning results

Status update: MSS clamp to 1360 applied 2026-09-03 09:35 PT and egress pinning active for the Sparrow subnets. Observations in 24h post-change:
- Failure rate for large responses dropped from ~3.1% to ~0.15%.
- No measurable impact on other tenants in the peering fabric.
- Orbital agreed to keep fragment-pass enabled for Sparrow while they schedule a security review; Sparrow proxy vendor will enable MSS clamping downstream as part of their config roll.

Next steps:
- Add explicit MTU/MSS validation into the private-deploy onboarding checklist and automation tests.
- Schedule joint remediation call with Orbital + Sparrow proxy vendor to harden reassembly/policy.

Thanks everyone for the quick coordination.

-Markus Klein
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
